paper.title: Generation through the Lens of Learning Theory
paper.summary: Studies uniform, nonuniform, and in-limit language generation through closure dimension and finite-cover characterizations, hierarchy separations, prompted generation, and learning-theoretic combinatorial parameters. The registry also separates false literal finite-universe readings, records a refutation of the printed arbitrary-class identification theorem and the printed streamwise-EUC equivalence, and limits Theorem 4.1 coverage to its VC/Littlestone combinatorial core.

formalization_scope.summary: The custom inventory contains twenty-two cross-edition claim groups. Lean fully covers fourteen, partially covers five claims whose printed countable-universe wording has a false finite-universe reading or whose learning-theory transports are absent, and covers none of three claims: printed Theorem 2.3, the source-only EUC-not-uniform separation, and the refuted arbitrary-stream EUC equivalence. Twenty-five canonical Lean endpoints are linked, including cross-paper identification bridges deliberately kept outside the P02 umbrella.
specializations: Proposition 2.1, Theorem 2.2, the infinite-prompt separation, and Lemma C.1 are formalized on explicit countably infinite universes. Their literal generic-countable wording is false on finite universes; Theorem 4.1 has the same finite-universe boundary.
Paper-facing ordinary and prompted characterization theorems make the source's implicit nonempty example universe explicit.
Theorem 4.1 is formalized only at the six-region VC/Littlestone combinatorial-characterization boundary. Literal PAC probability-space and online-regret transports are not present.
The formalization is semantic and generally noncomputable; it does not claim efficient learners, finite membership-query implementations, or computable real-valued probability distributions.
Finite histories are represented by ordered prefixes while closure witnesses use Finsets of distinct observations; Lean time is zero-based.
Corollary 5.3(ii)--(iii) is strengthened from countably infinite classes to all countable classes, and the quantitative post-Theorem-3.3 result is sharpened to the exact interval from C(H) to C(H)+1.
gaps: The literal arbitrary-class Theorem 2.3 is false without a countability or indexing hypothesis. Lean links a counterexample and a separately named countable correction, neither of which is counted as coverage of the refuted printed claim.
The literal PAC and online-learning transports needed to turn the Theorem 4.1 dimension landscape into the printed learning-theory theorem are outside the current Lean scope.
The source assertion that EUC does not imply uniform generation has no linked Lean theorem and has not received a source-faithfulness assessment.
The printed arbitrary-stream reformulation of EUC is false. Lean refutes it; the repaired Theorems C.2 and C.4 use Definition C.1 directly.

Only Proposition 2.1 and Theorems 2.4, 2.5, 3.3, 3.5, and 3.10 have named human correspondence review. The AI-assisted audit is pinned only to arXiv v5 and predates the current Theorem 2.2/2.3 bridge and refutation endpoints.

Definitions and results outside the declared custom source scope, proof-only helpers, individual Theorem 4.1 construction endpoints, oracle and efficiency remarks, and appendical proof intermediates are not independently carded.

claims.title: Printed arbitrary-class tell-tale characterization of identification
claims.statement_summary: The arXiv edition claims the tell-tale characterization for an arbitrary UUS hypothesis class, while the COLT edition states it for an arbitrary hypothesis class. Both omit a class-countability or indexed-family hypothesis and are false; the UUS counterexample linked below refutes both versions.

source_assessment.notes: Angluin's original indexed-family theorem has a countable range. The printed arbitrary-class restatement loses that hypothesis: an uncountable UUS inclusion antichain has empty tell-tales for every member but cannot be the range of a language-valued finite-history identifier over a countable universe.

claims.title: Optimal uniform generation sample complexity lies between closure dimension and its successor
